still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.
The April 2033 Section 232 tariff of 100% on finished peptide drugs and peptide APIs from China and India is still in force, and Novo's Danish and US plants and Lilly's US plants are still exempt.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 45.5% ever-used − 34.8% current = 10.7% of adults who used and are off now. About 50% of current users are on a second or later course (17.4 points), and 3.2 points cycled and are off again, so (17.4 + 3.2) / 45.5 ≈ 45.3% of ever-users have cycled. The other ~7.5 points stopped once and have not restarted. This is consistent with one-year persistence near one-third on cash weekly and oral products, ~60% inside conditioned tracks and on clinic-given MariTide, and 36–47% restarting within a year. The 2035 Wegovy-pill recall forced ~4.5M switches and ~0.9M stops, and about 60% of those who stopped had restarted by Dec 2036. The 10.9-point rise in ever-use comes from: longevity/'metabolic health' starts among people without obesity (~4.5 pts); track enrolment (~2.5); oral amycretin at $299 (~2); calm and compulsion plans (~1.2); AUD and gambling labels via Medicaid (~0.7). Age check: 0.20×22 + 0.33×37 + 0.24×48 + 0.23×29 = 4.4 + 12.21 + 11.52 + 6.67 = 34.8. The 65+ band grew most slowly (21.5 → 29) after the April 2035 bone communication. Income thirds average 34.8. Users: 34.8% of ~276M adults ≈ 96.0M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~24.0M (25%, of which ~14.5M are in conditioned tracks); Medicare ~15.5M (16%); Medicaid ~5.6M (5.8%; ~1.4M AUD, ~0.2M gambling since Feb 2036); legitimate cash ~45.0M (47%, including ~9M longevity users without obesity, ~4.6M calm/focus/compulsion subscribers and ~5M on indefinite starting doses); compounded, imported or counterfeit ~5.9M (6.1%). Sum: 24.0 + 15.5 + 5.6 + 45.0 + 5.9 = 96.0. About 11.5M users (~12%) have BMI under 27 and no diabetes. Adult obesity ~30.9%. About 18% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: 2.0% of under-18s are on a drug, ~3.8% of 12–17s and ~0.7% of 6–11s; ~62% of new 6–11 starts are Medicaid/CHIP under EPSDT. About 6.0M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~15.5M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) and AUD codes, all behind prior authorisation. Gambling disorder became a further code in Feb 2036. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 15.5M × ~$221 average net/month × 12 ≈ $41.1B gross Part D incretin spend (up from ~$38.3B). Dementia route: ~2.6M × $235 × 12 ≈ $7.3B. AUD route: ~1.1M × $200 × 12 ≈ $2.6B. The 2034 CMS AUD coding audit closed in Jun 2035 with ~$310M in Part D recoupments from two telehealth-heavy plan sponsors. Since Oct 2035 Part D plans must document a DXA within 12 months for users 65+ on drug more than 2 years. Bimagrumab is covered only under its restricted high-fracture-risk label. Medicaid (~5.6M): AUD and, from Feb 2036, gambling disorder are not weight-loss uses, so both are covered outpatient drugs in every state under existing rebate law. FICTIONAL: 5.6M × ~$190 net × 12 ≈ $12.8B. 7 states still cover adult weight-loss use and no state changed its policy. Children 6–11 reach semaglutide under EPSDT.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month in India and 100+ export markets. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $20–60 where patents are not enforced. Delivered to US addresses under the 2033 tariff and export-licence regime, the same product costs ~$90–180. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. A WTO panel on Beijing's complaint was constituted in 2035 and has not reported.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 38% of employers cover weight-management or 'metabolic' use, but ~74% of them use conditioned tracks requiring verified adherence, ≥5% loss or metabolic-marker progress, and since 2035 a lean-mass floor (InBody or DXA). Unconditional coverage is ~10% of employers. Tracks hold ~14.5M of ~24M commercial users, including ~2.5M members without obesity admitted on prediabetes, waist circumference or ApoB criteria. FEHB conditioned users ~0.8M. Prices in Dec 2036: after the July 2035 nitrosamine recall, Novo ended the $149 TrumpRx Wegovy-pill starting dose in Jan 2036 and replaced it with $199 starting and $249 maintenance. Lilly kept Foundayo's $149 starting dose but limited it to the first three fills, then $229, so $149 now buys only a start. Oral amycretin was listed on TrumpRx at $299 (Jan 2036, down from ~$449 cash). Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound cost $249–299, MariTide $249 direct (~7.1M users), retatrutide ~$399. 503A/503B compounded semaglutide was legal while semaglutide was on the shortage list (Aug 2035–Feb 2036) at $179–249; ~1.1M people still buy it under 'clinical difference' claims. The ~5M people on indefinite starting doses saw their monthly cost rise 34–54% ($149 to $199–229). Orals are ~62% of users: Foundayo ~23M, oral amycretin ~13M, Wegovy pill/Rybelsus ~23.5M.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity was reached in Feb 2034 with oral amycretin (~21.5% at 72 weeks). In this window it is realised through access rather than a new molecule. Oral amycretin was listed on TrumpRx at $299 in Jan 2036, absorbed Wegovy-pill patients displaced by the 2035 recall, and grew from ~2.2M to ~13M users. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%, and no new molecular entity was approved. The gambling-disorder sNDA for the Wegovy pill was filed Jan 2035 and approved Feb 2036 (13 months), on a 52-week trial showing ~38% fewer gambling days than placebo. Lilly resubmitted the tirzepatide dementia 60+ without-CVD extension in Mar 2035. The FDA issued a complete response letter in Dec 2035 citing the hip-fracture imbalance in women 70+. Lilly began a tirzepatide-plus-bimagrumab bone-protected trial (phase 3, no filing). Bimagrumab users ~0.6M under the restricted label. Implants remain in phase 1–2 and are not on the market. Global incretin market ~$235B (2035). US branded net prices on injectables still drift down 3–5% a year. Price rises in this step came in the starting-dose and shortage channels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside tracks. Forced switches after the 2035 recall caused a wave of re-titration nausea, and ~20% of switchers to oral amycretin quit within 3 months.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first two MDL bellwethers (Oct 2035, Mar 2036) split, with a defence verdict on persistence and a $4.1M plaintiff verdict on an ileus case. GI claims ~44,000.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling; further bellwethers set for 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low; still pleaded with EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss, population-level fracture burden in older and long-term users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The CMS/FDA Sentinel analysis (Apr 2035) found hip-fracture HR ~1.35 after 2+ years, ~1.5 after three or more cycles and ~1.6 in women 70+. That implies ~20,000 excess hip fractures a year among ~18M users 65+ (baseline ~4 per 1,000 person-years) and, at ~20% one-year post-fracture mortality, ~4,000 excess deaths. Regain after cycling is disproportionately fat ('sarcopenic regain'). Grip-strength decline is measurable in non-obese longevity users at 18 months.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Drug Safety Communication and class label update (Apr 2035): baseline DXA for users 65+ or on drug >2 years, resistance-training and protein counselling. Part D DXA documentation requirement from Oct 2035. CRL on the tirzepatide dementia extension. No boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including AUD-label and early gambling-label users.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 2033 FDA study found ~7% clinically meaningful anhedonia at maintenance doses vs ~3.5% in controls, ~10% on retatrutide. An NIH-funded low-dose cohort (Sep 2036) found ~4.6% vs ~3.6% at calm-plan doses, not statistically significant. Platforms quote it as clearance and critics as underpowered.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. The gambling label carries mood-monitoring counselling but no warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after cycles. ~0.9M stopped during the 2035 recall gap.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins conditioned coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine deficiency (AUD users who keep drinking). Protein insufficiency now reported in non-obese longevity users eating ~1,300 kcal/day.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language; thiamine counselling on AUD label; protein counselling added in Apr 2035 class update.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims ~71,000. DOJ civil investigative demand unresolved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled for semaglutide and tirzepatide. Novo's 2033 Form 483 closed in 2035 after remediation.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~14 years of semaglutide follow-up. Nobody has studied lifelong use in people without obesity, or indefinite starting-dose use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Reports tied to non-approved product passed ~39,000. The 2035–36 legal compounding window produced a dosing-error spike, with poison-centre calls up ~20% in Q4 2035. Domestic re-filling from smuggled API continues in the Gulf South. A second Burkholderia cluster (Louisiana, 2036) caused ~60 infections and 1 death.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Shortage-list compounding ended Feb 2036; FDA warning letters to 14 503A pharmacies over 'clinical difference' claims; no statute; no state action.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Height velocity ~0.5–0.6 cm/year below expected in prepubertal starters on either drug, with partial catch-up after stopping. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language and medication guide; no REMS; AAP keeps lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration)
Nitrosamine drug-substance-related impurity (NDSRI) in oral semaglutide tablets
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Found in Jul 2035 above FDA's acceptable intake in lots from one tableting line; theoretical lifetime cancer risk is small. Recall covered ~38% of US Wegovy-pill/Rybelsus supply for ~7 months.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class 2 recall, shortage listing Aug 2035–Feb 2036, reformulated process approved Jan 2036, nitrosamine testing on every lot.

food_and_beverage.state: About 52% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%. Longevity users without obesity are a new segment. They are affluent, eat little and buy protein and 'muscle-floor' lines, which Kraft Heinz and General Mills now plan around the lean-mass conditions in tracks. The 2033 'tariff bounce' in lower-income zips faded as starting-dose and Medicaid users increased. Grocery dollar sales are flat to slightly down.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~21% from 2025 and beer ~14%. Medicaid AUD coverage and EAP pill programmes keep eroding the heavy-drinking core. Bardstown-area distilleries cut ~1,200 more jobs, and two mid-sized Kentucky producers sold aged stock to Asian bottlers. Non-alcoholic drinks are ~6% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Late-night and bar revenue keeps falling in Dayton, Toledo and Columbus. Casual dining runs half-portion menus and 'protein plates' scaled to track floors. Casino buffets in Las Vegas and Atlantic City cut seating, while sportsbook bars convert to lounges.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Resale, stretch and size-flex subscriptions serve cyclers and the recall-gap regain. Structured athletic wear and tailoring keep growing. Petite sizing has expanded for longevity users 50+.

fitness.state: Lean-mass floors in tracks made strength training a coverage requirement. Budget chains sell 'track-compliant' InBody packages, and senior resistance programmes at YMCAs and Medicare Advantage gyms (SilverSneakers-type) roughly doubled enrolment after the April 2035 bone communication.

insurance.state: Employer coverage rose to 38%, ~74% of it conditioned, with lean-mass floors standard since PBMs' 2035 track products. Pharmacy trend ~+6%. Part D premiums rose again and plans added DXA documentation. Medicaid absorbs AUD and now gambling users without any state having chosen to. Life insurers ask applicants whether and why they stopped an incretin.

pharma.state: Still growing (~$235B global). Lilly gained most: Foundayo is a chemically synthesised small molecule, so it scaled while the peptide recall cut Novo's pill supply. Novo's oral amycretin recovered share at $299 on TrumpRx, but Novo lost ~$3B of 2035 revenue to the recall. Amgen grew on tracks. Litigation-finance firms shifted toward fracture claims. Indian exporters serve Gulf, Latin American and African markets.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on it is the default. In Columbus, Scottsdale and suburban Atlanta the question is which drug and which tier, not whether. Lean and scanned with good grip strength means covered and compliant. Thin and frail at 70 means someone skipped the DXA. A body that regained in 2035 still reads as 'recall year'. A body with obesity and no drug now reads as poor, rural or principled, and people ask which.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the class uniform, now formalised by lean-mass floors in tracks. The new elite body is 'metabolically optimised', a non-obese 55-year-old on a low-dose pill and a longevity clinic's protocol, and 'off-drug lean' has become a rarer, more defensive boast. Upper-income parents still largely refuse drugs for prepubertal children. Medicaid children remain most new 6–11 starts.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short, protein-heavy and documented. Bread Alone claims ~1,300 congregations, and its 'full table' suppers now draw grandparents worried about bones. Thanksgiving tables include the 'one who's off', whose plate is noticed.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps dropped most drug tags as nearly universal, keeping 'off by choice' and the 'calm/compulsion plan' tags. 'Off by choice' functions as a values disclosure. Couples sync pill windows. A partner who stops is now asked to explain, the way smoking used to be.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: For most of the insured middle, appetite is a managed variable like blood pressure. For longevity users without obesity it is a lifespan risk to be minimised. In the Delta and Memphis the 'hunger tax' language revived when the $149 semaglutide start ended. The 2034 backlash coalition fragmented. MAHA groups pivoted to the bone data ('Let Them Stand'), and Unmuted to the gambling label.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Maintenance-dose anhedonia ~7% vs ~3.5% (FDA 2033), ~10% on retatrutide. The NIH low-dose cohort (2036) found ~4.6% vs ~3.6%, not significant. ~4.6M people are on calm/focus/compulsion plans at $149–249 plus a $39–59 fee. About 40% are written on the AUD or gambling labels, and the rest are cash off-label. If a low-dose excess near one point is real, it amounts to ~46,000 subscribers.
interior_life.framing: Platforms sell 'quiet the noise', 'quiet the bottle' and, from 2035, 'quiet the bet' and 'quiet the cart'. Novo's gambling launch says 'fewer gambling days'. HR calls it steadiness and benefits brokers call it 'impulse-cost reduction'. Clinicians say dose-related blunting, and Unmuted says 'subscription sedation'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 14.5M employees are in conditioned tracks, and a missed log or a lean-mass scan below the floor can drop a family's premium tier for the year. EAPs at warehousing, trucking and call-centre firms offer the AUD and gambling labels. Casino and sportsbook operators in Las Vegas exclude their own employees' compulsion plans from coverage, citing conflicts. FMCSA is still silent on calm plans. The two EEOC charges remain unresolved.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account is down ~18% from 2033 in insured suburbs of Ohio and New Jersey, and operators shift marketing to low-income and uninsured zips. 'Dry' comedy has given way to 'off' comedy, about the one friend who stopped. Live-music nights in Columbus and Louisville keep shrinking. Streaming 'ambient' tiers bundle with calm subscriptions.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Pill windows structure mornings. Couples therapists now report 'mismatched tiers', where one partner's track compliance sets the family premium and the other partner's lapse costs money. Compulsion-plan users report less shopping and betting, and partners report less spontaneity, in roughly the same words.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No state acted, although Ohio and New Jersey sports-betting tax receipts fell ~9% and ~7% from peak. Congress held a hearing on the recall and the bone data without a bill. The end of the $149 semaglutide start revived the 'hunger tax' line in Mississippi and Tennessee campaigns. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal and routine. The FDA approved the gambling label, issued the April 2035 bone Safety Communication, ran the recall and shortage listing, opened and then closed the compounding window, and sent a CRL on the dementia extension. CMS closed its AUD audit with recoupments and added DXA documentation. No state legislature or agency acted. Illinois's ban is still the only one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new subsidy. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands. OPM kept FEHB conditions and added a lean-mass floor for plan year 2036. Medicaid gambling coverage became effectively mandatory under existing rebate law, as AUD had. Part D DXA documentation is a plan requirement.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Deeper and more physical. Track data now include body-composition scans, smart-bottle logs, PBM fills, telehealth mood check-ins and, in some tracks, grip-strength readings from gym kiosks. All of it flows to wellness vendors under consent. Gambling-label platforms ask for read access to sportsbook account history. Benefit brokers buy de-identified 'impulse' cohorts.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers AUD and gambling labels under existing rules. The Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion and now requires DXA at entry. FMCSA guidance covers on-label AUD use only.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The 2033 tariff and India's export checks remain. A WTO panel on China's complaint was constituted in 2035. The July 2035 recall showed that oral peptide supply depends on a few US and Danish tableting lines, because oral semaglutide uses ~50–100× more API per patient-month than weekly injection. Lilly's small-molecule supply was not affected. Smuggled API still feeds Gulf South re-filling.

events.event: Novo files the Wegovy pill for gambling disorder after a 52-week trial; within weeks two calm platforms launch 'quiet the bet' and 'quiet the cart' plans for sports bettors and compulsive shoppers

An FDA–CMS Sentinel analysis estimates ~20,000 excess hip fractures a year among older incretin users; FDA issues a class Safety Communication requiring baseline DXA for users 65+ or on drug over two years, and Part D plans add DXA documentation from October

Novo recalls oral semaglutide lots from one tableting line over a nitrosamine impurity; the FDA lists semaglutide in shortage, 4.5 million pill users are switched, about 0.9 million stop, and compounders are legally back in business until February

Express Scripts and Optum roll out standard 'metabolic tracks' for 2036 that require adherence logs and a lean-mass floor and admit members without obesity on ApoB or waist criteria; track enrolment reaches 14.5 million
events.driver: coverage_shift: mandate_or_conditioning; new_indications: longevity_wellness; state_action: none

events.event: As pill supply resumes, Novo ends the $149 TrumpRx Wegovy starting dose (now $199), Lilly limits Foundayo's $149 start to three fills, and oral amycretin is listed on TrumpRx at $299, making it the fastest-growing product in the class

FDA approves the Wegovy pill for moderate-to-severe gambling disorder; because it is not a weight-loss use, Medicaid in every state must cover it, and sportsbook operators report falling handle in insured suburbs

open_tensions: The bone data are now official, at ~20,000 excess hip fractures a year. Insurers answered with lean-mass floors that make muscle a condition of coverage, so the older users least able to build muscle are the likeliest to lose their tier. Bimagrumab stays restricted, and the FDA turned down tirzepatide's dementia extension over fractures in older women.

About 11.5 million people without obesity take incretins for 'metabolic health' and longevity. Track criteria built on ApoB and waist size, plus cash clinics, keep adding them. There are no outcome data for lifelong use in lean bodies, and early grip-strength and protein findings point the wrong way.

The recall showed that pill supply rests on a handful of peptide lines. It ended the $149 semaglutide start, raised costs 34–54% for ~5 million people on indefinite starting doses, and briefly legalised compounding. Back-room re-filling in the Gulf South never stopped.

Gambling disorder joined alcohol as a Medicaid-mandated label. Platforms now sell 'quiet the bet' and ask for sportsbook data. The low-dose anhedonia study came back ambiguous, and state betting revenue is falling while no state acts.

prose.headline: The Country That Stopped Asking: 96 Million Americans On, a Recall, a Bone Count, and a Pill for the Bet
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 a little over a third of American adults take an incretin drug, about ninety-six million people, and nearly half have tried one. The figure that matters socially is the inverse. Not being on one is now the thing people ask about, at work, on dating apps, and on life-insurance forms that want to know when and why you stopped.

The pill made this possible. Oral amycretin, approved in 2034 with the weight loss of the injectables, was listed on the TrumpRx cash channel at $299 in January 2036 and became the fastest-growing product in the class. Lilly's small-molecule Foundayo is the volume workhorse. Most users swallow rather than inject, and the clinic bruise is becoming a sign of an older regimen.

The pill also showed its fragility. In July 2035 Novo recalled oral semaglutide made on one tableting line after a nitrosamine impurity turned up above the federal limit. The tablet needs far more drug substance per patient than a weekly shot, and there was no spare capacity. The FDA declared a shortage, four and a half million people were switched, and almost a million simply stopped. For seven months compounding pharmacies could legally sell semaglutide again, and poison-centre calls rose. When supply came back in January, Novo dropped the $149 starting dose that six million people had been living on and set a $199 floor. Lilly kept its $149 Foundayo start but limited it to three fills. In Jackson and Memphis the old phrase for this, the hunger tax, came back into campaign speeches.

Coverage grew and tightened. Thirty-eight percent of employers now pay, and three-quarters of them run tracks. In late 2035 the two largest pharmacy-benefit managers made these a standard product. You log every dose, you hit your loss or your cholesterol target, and since this year you keep your muscle above a floor measured on a body-composition scale at the gym. Fourteen and a half million workers live inside these tracks. Some of them are not obese at all. They are admitted on cholesterol particle counts or waist size, and they joined a cash market of affluent forty-to-seventy-year-olds who take the drugs for what clinics call metabolic health. About eleven and a half million users now have no obesity and no diabetes.

The muscle floor exists because of the bones. In April 2035 a federal analysis of Medicare data put the excess at about twenty thousand hip fractures a year among older users. Women over seventy and people who had cycled on and off were worst affected. The FDA told prescribers to scan bone density at baseline, Medicare drug plans began demanding the scan, and YMCA strength classes for seniors doubled. In December the agency rejected Lilly's bid to market tirzepatide for dementia prevention to healthy sixty-year-olds, citing the same fractures. The cash clinics kept prescribing it.

The drug's reach into craving widened. In February 2036 the Wegovy pill was approved for gambling disorder. Medicaid must cover it everywhere, for the same reason it had to cover the alcohol label: it is not a weight-loss use. The telehealth calm platforms had already launched plans to quiet the bet and the shopping cart, and about 4.6 million people subscribe to one plan or another. A federal study of low doses found a small excess of anhedonia that was not statistically significant. Sportsbook handle per account is falling in the insured suburbs of Ohio and New Jersey, and the operators are moving their advertising to the zip codes without coverage. State betting revenue is down, and no state has done anything about it.

The spirits volume keeps falling, and Bardstown keeps shedding jobs. Restaurants serve smaller plates with more protein. Bread Alone's suppers draw grandparents now. From the outside the country looks lean, sober, steady and well measured, and the measurements are where its life now happens.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalczyk sets the bottle on the counter at 5:40. It is oral amycretin, through the hospital's metabolic track, $25 a month. She has taken it since last August, when the pharmacy said her old pill was recalled. The cap's ring turns green. Thirty minutes until coffee.

She uses the time to text her mother's rehab unit. The right hip is pinned and she might bear weight Thursday. The surgeon asked how long she'd been on tirzepatide, wrote down eleven years, and didn't say anything else.

At work in Columbus she codes claims for orthopaedics. Every third chart, she notices, lists a DXA.

At lunch she walks to the gym across from the parking garage for her quarterly scan. She steps onto the InBody plate barefoot and holds the handles. Skeletal muscle is 24.1 kilos, three-tenths over her floor. The kiosk asks if she wants to share the result with Anthem. It isn't really a question. She taps yes.

Her husband Gary texts a photo of the pharmacy screen: Foundayo, $229. His three cheap fills are used up. He writes "lol" and she knows he means it isn't funny.

At dinner their son Tyler, twenty-four, eats a second piece of bread. He's been off since spring. Gary asks if it's the money. Tyler says no, he just wants to be hungry. Nobody says anything. Denise watches him butter it.

At nine she does the band exercises the app assigns, forty rows on the door handle, and logs them. The phone gives her a gold check.
